steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease cookie sheets.

In a medium bowl, stir peanut butter and sugar together until smooth. Beat in the eggs, one at a time, then stir in the baking soda, salt, and vanilla. Roll dough into 1 inch balls and place them 2 inches apart onto the prepared cookie sheets. Press a criss-cross into the top using the back of a fork.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes in the preheated oven. Allow cookies to cool on baking sheet for 5 minutes before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Peanut Butter Cookies Ever

review.reviewBody: This is a great recipes but I did make a few revisions to make it even better. Instead of two cup white sugar I used 1 cup white and one cup brown, I also only used used one tsp baking powder. The recipe creates a firm dough and maintains is "criss cross" shape. well. This one is a keeper! Thanks!

I have been making these cookies for a few years now and some of my friends actually beg me to make them - they are the tastiest peanut butter cookies ever. When I first started making them I read some of the other reviews and made some slight adjustments - I use organic peanut butter ( a must) as it has that extra oil that make the cookies more moist. I use 1 cup of white sugar and 1 cup of brown (although you could probably use a little less of the white). I also mix the baking soda with a little warm water before mixing it is so it doesn't clump (very little, like a teaspoon full) The best part though - I mix about 1 cup of Reese's Peanut Butter Chips in as well. These are the best cookies ever - just saying. Also, just before putting them in the oven I put a little extra salt ( I use Pink Himalayan Salt) on top - so good!! Enjoy :)

These are super easy, use just a few ingredients, and really satisfy a peanut butter cookie craving! I made half a recipe because I didn't need a lot of cookies.... Used up some creamy peanut butter and then added some crunchy to equal one cup....Used half white and half brown sugar, and added a little extra vanilla. Rolled the cookie balls in granulated sugar, did the crisscross and baked - yum!! The dough came together great to roll the cookies....just be careful when removing from the baking sheets. I had one cookie casualty due to me removing fron cookie sheet to the cooling rack too soon before the cookies had set.... of course that was great for a taste test! :)

OMG, best peanut butter cookies I've ever baked! I'll never make peanut butter cookies with flour again! If you prefer a chewy, creamy, not super-sweet PB cookies, these are for you. I took several suggestion from previous comments and used a full 18 oz. jar of Jiff Natural PB, omitted the salt, and modified the sugar to 1 c. brown sugar and 1/2 c. white sugar. I also chilled the dough for an hour before scooping, which made it very easy to get them on the cookie sheets and gently fork-flatten them. Definitely let them cool on the cookie sheets themselves until they set. SO EASY AND YUMMO--MAKE THESE NOW!!! :-D
Pure sugar goodness. These were super good. Pulled from oven after 10 minutes, topped with a few semi chocolate chips, baked for another minute, what a yummy sugar high. Easy and so good.

Incredibly delicious and easy!! Bake them as follows and they will come out soft and yummy!! Key is not to bake very long…maybe 4 mins and then let them finish baking on the hot cookie sheet on the cooling rack to finish up otherwise they will be crumbly and dry.

As a diabetic, I changed the 2 cups of sugar to 2 cups of truvia, and they were amazing. I had tried with splenda, but the splenda does not mix as well because it is not granulated. I am thinking of reducing the truvia to 1 1/2 cups next time I make them, I think they will still be fantastic!

I've made these cookies a couple times and they are super easy and so delicious. Some revisions though. I used a jar of extra chunky peanut butter. 1 cup sugar/1 cup brown sugar. Added 2t of almond extract . No need to use a fork. they flatten out just fine on their own. Bake 7 minutes with small cookie scoop

Far too sweet. Probably should have chosen a different recipe. However, if you are keen to try one without flour as I was decrease the amount of sugar, more salt, use unsweetened peanut butter, don't exceed 8 minutes cook time. Definitely let cool on baking sheet. These won't be disappearing quickly...FYI tried twice to upload a photo but it wants me to adjust pixels and I don't feel like it.

Tops for peanut butter lovers! I made these with one cup sugar and one cup brown sugar as suggested in the first review. I also used premium brand name peanut butter. Delicious!! Please note these are very fragile when they come out of the oven and need to cool on the pan for a few minutes, before moving to a rack. Enjoy!!

Amazing, and spectacular recipe really easy; however, I would recommend cooking for 10-12 minutes, and adding vanilla extract and salt just for more of a flavorful balance. Also adding a little crunchy peanut butter with the creamy adds a cool texture!

I made it exactly per the recipe and they came out perfectly—would repeat! I used 100% real peanut butter with no additives—many products sold as "peanut butter" have added sweeteners, hydrogenated oils, stabilizers, etc. which may be the reason for some issues mentioned in the comments.
I love peanut butter cookies and have tried many different recipes This one was the worst. It was a waste of good peanut butter. .
Good instead of the criss cross we used a leaf cookie cutter to make it feel more like Fall.
I signed up for this just to review these cookies! We are obsessed. Besides the cookies coming out amazing it's just such an easy recipe. I would give it more stars if I could

Terribly disappointed! While the flavor was good, these cookies completely crumbled when cooled. If feel like the lack of flour contributed to this. They were incredibly greasy which I expected with the amount of peanut butter, but while removing from cookie sheets, to cooling racks, they just fell apart. I let them cool completely, and the cooled cookies just crumble in your hands. So disappointed!
I used 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup brown sugar and kept everything else the same. They were delicious! I will definitely be making these again. Everyone enjoyed them.

Best recipe ever; I've used it for 50 years !! This is nearly the same recipe my mom found in 50s or 60s in Woman's Day or Family Circle, but no baking powder or soda. The trick to dryness is to not overbake. Use with chocolate kisses or morsels for Christmas.
I used crunchy peanutbutter and everybody loved them!
